With reference to the arrest of two staff members
of the now defunct local Kuomintang headquarters on
March 15, 1938, at No.17, Lane 252, Route Pere Robert,
at the request of the Japanese Authorities on suspicion
of being engaged in anti-Japanese terroristic activities
(Vide Central Misc. 307/38), the following particulars of
the prisoners are on the records of this section :-
(1) Loh Ying Chu (陸蔭初).
Loh Ying Chu, aged 34, native of Tsungming, joined
the local Kuomintang headquarters as a clerk in 1931, and
a few years later became one of the staff members of the
People's Movement Training Committee, which position he
held up to the time of the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in Shanghai in August, 1937. He was never
heard of again until his arrest.
As the People's Movement Training Committee of the
Kuomintang Headquarters undertook the registration of
public bodies and the supervision of their activities,
Mr. Loh Ying Chu's activities were confined to the
direction of the movements of a number of labour unions
and participated in mediations in labour disputes including
the following :-
a) Strike in Foh Sing Cigarette Factory (Chinese concern)
in connection with the enforcement of a labour agreement
in February, 1936.
b) Strike of mechanics and coolies of the Shanghai Electric
Construction Company (British) in March, 1937, to
enforce a demand for the reinstatement of two dismissed
coolies.
c) Strike of chauffeurs of the Ford Hire Service in
April, 1937. (American concern)

关于1938年3月15日，应日本当局请求，以涉嫌从事反日恐怖活动为由，
逮捕两名现已解散的当地国民党总部职员一事（见中央杂项档案 307/38），
逮捕地点为贝当路 (Route Pere Robert) 252弄17号，
本处档案中有关囚犯的详情如下：
(1) 陸蔭初 (Loh Ying Chu)。
陸蔭初，34岁，崇明人，1931年作为职员加入当地国民党总部，
几年后成为民众运动训练委员会的工作人员之一，该职位他一直担任至
1937年8月上海中日战事爆发时。此后直至被捕，杳无音信。
由于国民党总部的民众运动训练委员会负责公共团体的登记及其活动的监督，
陸蔭初先生的活动仅限于指导一些工会的运动，并参与调解劳资纠纷，包括以下案件：
a) 1936年2月，福兴香烟厂（华商）因执行劳工协议而发生的罢工。
b) 1937年3月，上海电力建设公司（英商）的技工和苦力为要求复职两名被解雇的苦力而举行的罢工。
c) 1937年4月，福特租车行（美商）司机的罢工。

        Mr. Loh was one of the promoters of the "Peasants

Headquarters for the proclaimed purpose of promoting the
welfare of labourers and peasants but little or nothing
was actually done.

and ceased functioning following the outbreak of the
Sino-Japanese hostilities.    This association was under
the influence of the General Labour Union and the Kuomintang

the workers of the Toyoda Cotton Mills (Japanese concerns).

Mills attacked the Jessfield Branch Police Station owing

March 16, 1938.
Afternoon Translation.

Eastern Times and other local newspapers:

ARREST OF A FORMER GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE IN FRENCH
CONCESSION

Shortly after 7 a.m. yesterday, detectives
and uniformed men of the Settlement Police, including
Japanese police officers, approached the French Police and
requested assistance in effecting the arrest of a Chinese
in Chuin Yien Villa (群賢別墅), Route Pere Robert, French
Concession.
The French Police detailed detectives and
uniformed men to accompany the officers of the Settlement
Police to the first floor of House No.17 Chuin Yien Villa,
where a man named Chu (朱), native of Nanking, was arrested
and a quantity of letters and other documents was seized.
It is learned that the arrested person was
formerly in the employ of the National Government at Nanking
but is now unemployed. The cause of his arrest is
unknown.

(批：C.Y.)

Tsang Sung ( 曾松 ), alias Tsong Ts'oo
( 曾松 )
Shanghai                                     Clerk Liao Chung Chien
Police Hdqrs.           16/3/38

My name is Tsang Sung, alias Tsong Ts'oo. I am a
native of Shanghai, aged 32, unemployed, at present residing
at 17 Chung Hsien Chun Terrace, Route Pere Robert.

I joined the Shanghai Kuomintang Headquarters in 1929 as
a clerk and held this position up to November, 1937, when
the Tangpu was dissolved as a result of the withdrawal of the
Chinese troops from this area. While in the Tangpu, my job
was to undertake various affairs in connection with the
registration of public organizations.

I did not meet any of the senior members of the Tangpu
since the dissolution of the organ; all of them are presumably
to have left for inland places.

After having been thrown out of employment, I used to
remain at home and had never participated in any political
movement or terroristic activities. I don't know any Korean
nor had I instructed any of my acquaintances to engage one to
throw bomb to threaten Japanese.

I understand that many persons bear grudge against me
because while I was in the employ of the Tangpu I used to be
strict in carrying out my duty.

Lau Ying Tsu ( 劉英柱 ) was formerly an office-mate of
mine in the Tangpu. He was discharged by the Kuomintang
Headquarters in August, 1937 when the organ, in effecting
economy, dispensed with the services of half of its staff.
Lau is at present employed with the Min Lih Middle School for
Girls and is residing with me at 17 Chung Hsien Chun Terrace,
Route Pere Robert.

(Signed) Tsang Sung.

曾松 (Tsang Sung)，别名 曾松 (Tsong Ts'oo)
上海                                     职员 廖仲坚
警察总局           1938年3月16日

我叫曾松，别名曾松。我是上海人，32岁，失业，
现居住在贝当路 (Route Pere Robert) 忠贤村露台17号。

我于1929年加入上海国民党总部担任职员，
一直任职至1937年11月，当时因中国军队撤离该地区，党部解散。
在党部任职期间，我的工作是处理与公共组织登记有关的各项事务。

自该机构解散以来，我未见过党部的任何高级成员；
推测他们均已前往内地。

失业后，我通常待在家里，从未参与任何政治运动或恐怖主义活动。
我不认识任何朝鲜人，也没有指示我的任何熟人雇佣他人
投掷炸弹以威胁日本人。

我知道许多人对我怀恨在心，因为我在党部任职期间
严格执行职责。

Lau Ying tsu (陸蔭初)
Tsungming                                      Clerk Liao Chung Chien
Police Hdqrs.              16/3/38

My name is Lau Ying tsu. I am a native of Tsungming,
aged 34, residing at 17 Chung Hsien Chun Terrace (賢別墅),
Route Pere Robert. I am at present employed as a clerk
with the Library of the Min Lih Middle School for Girls,
1192 Avenue Joffre.

In 1931 I joined the Kuomintang Headquarters as a clerk
in the General Affairs Department. In 1936 I was transferred
to the People's Training Department of the same organ. These
two departments dealt chiefly with the local labour disputes.
While in the Tangpu, I was sometimes instructed by the organ
to participate in mediating labour disputes in various factories
in Shanghai.

On August 11, 1937, I obtained leave from the Tangpu and
returned to Tsungming with my wife and three sons, the situation
in Shanghai at that time being tense.

On October 28, 1937, I alone came to Shanghai and learned
that my service with the Tangpu had been dispensed with. The
Tangpu, following the outbreak of the local hostilities in
August, 1937, discharged half of its staff as a measure in
effecting economy. As far as I know the Tangpu was dissolved
in November 1937 after the withdrawal of the Chinese forces
from Shanghai, and the services of all its staff were dispensed
with at the same time.

On February 1, 1938, I obtained my present employment with
the Min Lih Middle School for Girls.

On February 5, 1938, my mother-in-law died in Tsungming
and I immediately returned to my native home. I remained there

陆荫初 (Lau Ying tsu)
崇明                                      职员 廖仲坚
警察总局              1938年3月16日

我叫陆荫初。我是崇明人，
现年34岁，居住在倍尔路（Route Pere Robert）17号贤别墅（Chung Hsien Chun Terrace）。我目前受雇于
霞飞路1192号民立女子中学图书馆，担任职员。

1931年，我进入国民党总部，在总务部担任职员。1936年，我被调至
同一机构的民众训练部。这两个
部门主要处理当地的劳资纠纷。
在党部工作期间，我有时奉命参与调解上海各工厂的劳资纠纷。

1937年8月11日，我向党部请假，鉴于当时上海局势紧张，我与妻子和三个儿子返回了崇明。

1937年10月28日，我独自来到上海，得知我在党部的职务已被解除。自1937年8月当地战事爆发后，党部为节约开支，裁减了一半的工作人员。据我所知，随着中国军队从上海撤退，党部于1937年11月解散，所有工作人员的职务也同时被解除。

1938年2月1日，我获得了目前在民立女子中学的职位。

1938年2月5日，我的岳母在崇明去世，我立即返回家乡。我留在那里

page_data.en:
- 2 -

there until March 5 when I came to Shanghai together with
my wife.

I have been living with Tsang Sung ( 张 松 ), who was
one of my office-mates in the Tangpu, at 17 Chung Hsien Chun
Terrace, Route Pere Robert, since December, 1937.

I did not meet any of the senior members of the Tangpu
since the withdrawal of Chinese troops from Shanghai. I do
not know their present whereabouts.

After leaving the Tangpu, I had never participated in
any political movement and had never taken part in terroristic
activities. I don't know any Korean nor had I instructed any
of my acquaintances to engage one to throw bomb to threaten
Japanese.

(Signed) Lau Ying Tsu.

- 2 -

直到3月5日，我才与妻子一同来到上海。

自1937年12月以来，我一直与张松 (Tsang Sung) 同住，他是我在党部时的同事之一，住址为倍尔路17号贤别墅。

自中国军队从上海撤退后，我再未见过党部的任何高级成员。我不知道他们目前的下落。

离开党部后，我从未参与过任何政治运动，也从未参加过恐怖活动。我不认识任何朝鲜人，也没有指示任何熟人雇佣他人投掷炸弹以威胁日本人。

Date August 1, 19 38.

Subject FURTHER TO REPORT ON ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.

Made by D.S. BRADLEY Forwarded by D.I. GLOVER.

Sir,

Zung Moo Ding, who was handed over to the Japanese Military Police at 12 noon 6.7.38, was released by them on 23/7/38. No report of his release was made by the Japanese Military Police.

On 26.7.38 Zung Moo Ding came to C.B.H.Q. to collect his property and he stated that he had been taken over the Soochow Creek and lodged in a cell in a building which he did not know.

The same questions that were put to him by the Japanese Military Police and detectives attached to C.I. whilst he was in custody at C.B.H.Q. were put to him whilst he was in his cell and he gave the same answers.

It seems strange that Zung Moo Ding, who had been held in Police custody from 14.6.38 to 6.7.38 whilst enquiries were being made by the Japanese Military, should be released by them despite the fact that they came to Police Headquarters with a despatch from Kiangyin, stating that he was definitely wanted by the Japanese Military in Kiangyin.

Zung Moo Ding at no time left Hongkew from the day of handing over till his release.

Zung Moo Ding stated that he had heard from a friend that his "expenses" during his stay in Hongkew amounted to $2000 and that sum had been paid prior to his release. It is not known who received the $2000 as Zung Moo Ding stated that his friend had paid the money. Zung Moo Ding has now left for Kiangyin.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

先生，

戎满庭 (Zung Moo Ding) 于1938年7月6日中午12时被移交给日本宪兵队，并于1938年7月23日被他们释放。日本宪兵队未对其释放作出报告。

1938年7月26日，戎满庭来到刑事科总局领取其财物，他声称自己被带过苏州河，关押在一栋他不知道名称的建筑的牢房里。

当他在刑事科总局被拘留时，日本宪兵队和附属的情报科侦探向他提出的问题，在他被关押在牢房期间再次向他提出，而他给出了相同的回答。

奇怪的是，戎满庭在1938年6月14日至1938年7月6日期间因日本军方进行调查而被警方拘留，尽管日本军方带着来自江阴的公文来到警察总局，声明日本军方在江阴确实在通缉他，但他仍被日本军方释放。

从被移交到获释期间，戎满庭从未离开过虹口。

戎满庭称，他从一位朋友那里听说，他在虹口期间的“费用”共计2000美元，这笔钱在他获释前已支付。由于戎满庭称是他的朋友支付了这笔钱，因此不知是谁收到了这2000美元。戎满庭现已前往江阴。

此致，
敬礼，

native of Pau Koh, Kiangyin taken by D.S. Bradley.

My name is Wong Si Yah and I am a native of Pau Koh
18 miles from Kiangyin where I earn my living as an artist.
About February 1938 I left Pau Koh and came to Shanghai
to find employment. I have not found employment and
am at present residing with my brother-in-law named Tsang
Pau 〔此处转录不清〕 at No.7, Lane 274 Chengtu Road.

I was in the company of the other 3 arrested because
I received a telephone call from Lieu Ong Zung on 12.6.38,

I have known Lieu Ong Zung and Wong Tsoong Zung, who is
my nephew, since childhood but I only met Zung Moo Ding
for the 1st time in the Grand Hotel on 12.6.38.

Lieu Ong Zung is an oil dealer and Wong Tsoong Zung
is a sauce shop proprietor in Pau Koh Village.

I know nothing of Zung Moo Ding except what I have
told you.

I have never been concerned in Military affairs. I
ran away from Pau Koh into the country during the fighting,
but returned there when the fighting had subsided. I also
came to Shanghai because of the unsettled conditions and I
intend to remain here.

My name is Lieu Ong Zung, residing at Pau Koh Village,
18 miles from Kiangyin, and I carry on business as an oil
merchant dealing chiefly in Diesel Oil.

I left Pau Koh with Zung Moo Ding and Wong Tsung Zung
to proceed to Shanghai to buy oil on 9.6.38, and travelled
by the S.S. Dong Jan from Kiangyin, arriving in Shanghai at
7 p.m. 11.6.38.

All three of us engaged a room in the Grand Hotel, Yu Ya
Ching Road. On 12.6.38. I telephoned a friend named Wong Si Yeh
who lived in Shanghai and he came on the morning of 12.6.38,
and joined us. During that day we enjoyed ourselves and
I also transacted my oil business ordering 30 tons of oil for
myself and 2 tons of oil for Zung Moo Ding. I bought the
oil from an A.P.C. salesman named Koo through the agency of a
friend of mine named Pu To Ching ( ) who is at present
escorting 30 tons of oil to Kiangyin.

On the morning of 13.6.38. Won Si Yeh and myself proceeded
to the China Hotel Kweichow Road and engaged room 316. Wong Si
Yeh signed the name of Wu Ming on the register and he explained
when I asked him that Wu Ming was the person who introduced
him to the China Hotel.

I have known Zung Moo Ding for about 3 years, having
been introduced to him in Soochow by Wong Tsung Zung who
is a relative of mine.

I only know Zung Moo Ding by that name and I know of no
alias which he may be known.

The following is the statement of Wong Tsung Sung (王宗松) 28.
native of Kiangyin ........................................ taken by me D.S. Bradley.
at C.B.H.... on the 14/6/38 ........ and interpreted by D.J.I. Chu.

My name is Wong Tsung Sung, and I am a sauce shop master
in the village of Pu Koh about 18 miles from Kiangyin.

I came to Shanghai to see Lung Li Yeh to confer with
him regarding family matter and I left Pu Koh village on
9.6.38 in the company of Lieu Ong Lung and Lung Hoo Ding who
were also proceeding to Shanghai on business.

We travelled from Kiangyin on the S.S. Tung Ju and
arrived in Shanghai on 11/6/38, at 7 p.m. We then proceeded
to the Grand Hotel and engaged room 234.

On 12.6.38 we were joined by Lung Li Yeh and we spent
the day enjoying ourselves and also in transacting some
business.

We transferred to room 516 of the China Hotel on the morning of 13.6.38 and it was in this room that we were arrested.
We intended to return to Pu Koh within the next few days when
we had completed our business. I have known Lung Hoo Ding for
5 years and we were at the Tung Ching Primary School together.
When Lung Hoo Ding was a student he was known to the rest
of us as Li Yoong and he is commonly named Hoo Ding.

I only know Lung Hoo Ding as a farmer and pumping
contractor and know nothing of any other of his activities.
I have never been concerned in Military activities.

以下为王宗松（Wong Tsung Sung），28岁，江苏江阴人，于1938年6月14日在中央捕房（C.B.H.）由本人 D.S. Bradley 录取、并由 D.J.I. Chu 翻译的供词。

我叫王宗松，是距江阴约18英里的蒲港村的一名酱园店主。

我来上海是为了见龙立业（Lung Li Yeh），与他商议家事。我于1938年6月9日与刘翁龙（Lieu Ong Lung）和龙厚丁（Lung Hoo Ding）一同离开蒲港村，他们也是去上海做生意的。

我们乘坐“同聚”轮（S.S. Tung Ju）从江阴出发，于1938年6月11日晚7点抵达上海。随后我们前往大华饭店（Grand Hotel），入住了234号房间。

1938年6月12日，龙立业加入我们要，我们度过了一天，既娱乐也办理了一些业务。

1938年6月13日上午，我们转至中国饭店（China Hotel）的516号房间，我们就在该房间被捕。我们打算在办完事后的几天内返回蒲港。我认识龙厚丁已有5年，我们曾一起在同济小学（Tung Ching Primary School）读书。龙厚丁当学生时，我们其他人都叫他李勇（Li Yoong），他的常用名是厚丁（Hoo Ding）。

我只知道龙厚丁是个农民和抽水承包商，对他的其他活动一无所知。我从未参与过任何军事活动。

The following is the statement of Ung Hoo Ding ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ) 27.
native of 〔此处转录不清〕 taken by me D. B. Bradley.
at C.B.H. on the 14.6.38 and interpreted by D. I. Chu.

My name is Ung Hoo Ding, 27, native of Mingyin and I reside permanently in Gen On Teen some 60 Li from Mingyin City. I am a farmer but I have a sideline in contracting to pump water for my neighbours because I have a pump which works with Diesel oil fuel.

I never left my village during the trouble and the Japanese have never interfered with our village.

My reason for coming to Shanghai is because I wished to buy cheap Diesel oil for I understood that oil can be bought cheaper in Shanghai than in Mingyin.

I left Mingyin with two companions named Wong Teung Sung and Lieu Ong Zung and after we arrived in Mingyin we boarded a Portuguese owned steamship named the Dong Ju which transported us to the Bund, Shanghai; we arrived in Shanghai at about 7 p.m. 11.6.38 and Lieu Ong Zung, who was a little more acquainted with Shanghai than Wong Teung Sung and myself, took us to the Grand Hotel, Yu Y Ching Road, where we engaged a room.

We stayed 2 nights in the Grand Hotel. On 12.6.38 a friend of Wong Teung Sung named Wong Si Yah came to our room and on hearing that we were paying more than $3.00 per day for our room suggested that we should move to a cheaper place. We agreed and on the forenoon of 13.6.38 Wong Si Yah and Lieu Ong Zung proceeded to the China Hotel, Kweichow Road and engaged Room 316 in the name of Au Ming. I do not know why they registered in that name as I was still in the Grand Hotel when the room was engaged.

以下为 Ung Hoo Ding（〔此处转录不清〕），27岁，籍贯〔此处转录不清〕，于1938年6月14日在中央捕房（C.B.H.）由本人 D. B. Bradley 录取、并由 D. I. Chu 翻译的供词。

我叫 Ung Hoo Ding，27岁，籍贯明阴（Mingyin），常住于距明阴城约60里的根安甸（Gen On Teen）。我是个农民，但我有个副业，就是为邻居承包抽水工作，因为我有一台使用柴油燃料的水泵。

在事变期间我从未离开过村庄，日本人也从未干扰过我们的村子。

我来上海的原因是想购买便宜的柴油，因为我听说上海的油价比明阴便宜。

我和两位名叫 Wong Teung Sung 和 Lieu Ong Zung 的同伴一起离开明阴，到达明阴后，我们登上了一艘葡萄牙所有的名为“东聚”（Dong Ju）的轮船，它将我们运送到上海外滩；我们于1938年6月11日晚7点左右抵达上海。Lieu Ong Zung 比 Wong Teung Sung 和我更熟悉上海一些，他带我们去了虞洽卿路（Yu Y Ching Road）的大华饭店（Grand Hotel），并在那里开了一间房。

我们在大华饭店住了两晚。1938年6月12日，Wong Teung Sung 的一位名叫 Wong Si Yah 的朋友来到我们的房间，听说我们每天的房费超过3美元，便建议我们搬到一个更便宜的地方。我们同意了。1938年6月13日上午，Wong Si Yah 和 Lieu Ong Zung 前往贵州路的中国饭店（China Hotel），以 Au Ming 的名义预订了316号房间。我不知道他们为何用那个名字登记，因为订房时我还在大华饭店。

I can account for the envelope bearing the name **〔此处转录不清〕**
Yung being found in my possession. About 10 days ago whilst
I was in Cen 'on Tsen, a neighbour named Licu Ling Yuk (
farmer, became aware of my intention to visit another village
named via Leung and he asked me to deliver a letter to his
friend Licu Z Yoong , a shopkeeper who was doing business
in that village.

I agreed to deliver the letter and when I delivered it
to Licu Z Yoong he opened it, read the contents and threw
away the envelope. As the envelope could be used by me to
hold my money, I picked up the envelope. That it was how
it came to be in my possession when I was arrested.

I have no other name but Lung Koo Ding.

在我们住进那家酒店的房间后，居住在上海的 ng Ji Y h 带我们去 C.U.A. 咖啡馆吃早餐，吃完后他便离开了我们，而我和另外两人则去购物。

我已经通过 Licu Ong Sung 买到了我来上海要买的油，他在油商那里有些信用。我不认识那位油商，因为我把交易完全交给了 Licu。我已订购了两吨油，运往我的村庄 S.O.B.。

我可以解释为何在我身上发现了一个写有 **〔此处转录不清〕** Yung 名字的信封。大约10天前，当我在 Cen 'on Tsen 时，一位名叫 Licu Ling Yuk（农民）的邻居得知我打算去另一个名为 via Leung 的村庄，他便请求我送一封信给他的朋友 Licu Z Yoong，那是一位在该村经商的店主。

我同意送信，当我把信交给 Licu Z Yoong 时，他拆开信，读了内容，然后把信封扔掉了。因为那个信封可以用来装钱，我便捡起了信封。这就是我被捕时信封在我身上的由来。

我除了 Lung Koo Ding 之外没有其他名字。
我从未参与过任何军事活动。
